elements.requirement: Where a summons has been issued under section 1 and a magistrates' court has begun to try the information, the accused may at any time during or after the trial make a statutory declaration stating that the accused did not know of the summons or the proceedings until a specified date that falls after the court began to try the information.
elements.quote: the accused, at any time during or after the trial, makes a statutory declaration that he did not know of the summons or the proceedings until a date specified in the declaration, being a date after the court has begun to try the information

elements.requirement: The summons and all subsequent proceedings shall be void without prejudice to the validity of the information if the accused serves the statutory declaration on the designated officer for the court within 21 days of the specified date.
elements.quote: within 21 days of that date the declaration is served on the designated officer for the court, without prejudice to the validity of the information, the summons and all subsequent proceedings shall be void

elements.requirement: A statutory declaration is deemed duly served on the designated officer if it is delivered to the designated officer, left at the designated officer's office, or sent addressed to the designated officer at that office in a registered letter or by recorded delivery service.
elements.quote: deemed to be duly served on the designated officer if it is delivered to him, or left at his office, or is sent in a registered letter or by the recorded delivery service addressed to him at his office

elements.requirement: A magistrates' court, which may consist of a single justice, may accept service of the statutory declaration after the 21-day period has expired if on the application of the accused it appears that it was not reasonable to expect the accused to serve it within that period.
elements.quote: If on the application of the accused it appears to a magistrates’ court (which for this purpose may be composed of a single justice) that it was not reasonable to expect the accused to serve such a statutory declaration as is mentioned in subsection (1) above within the period allowed by that subsection, the court may accept service of such a declaration by the accused after that period has expired

elements.requirement: A statutory declaration accepted by the court after the expiry of the allowed period is deemed to have been served as required by subsection (1).
elements.quote: a statutory declaration accepted under this subsection shall be deemed to have been served as required by that subsection

elements.requirement: Where any proceedings have become void under subsection (1), the information shall not be tried again by any of the same justices.
elements.quote: Where any proceedings have become void by virtue of subsection (1) above, the information shall not be tried again by any of the same justices

thresholds.what: the period following the date specified in the declaration within which the statutory declaration must be served on the designated officer for the court
